cases.evidence: Piece ended on the disease NP and the emitted text omitted/rewrote the verb 'discovered', producing a translation that made the NP look like the subject.
cases.proposed_rule: Do not end a piece that isolates a noun phrase which is the complement/object of a preceding finite verb; keep that finite verb and its object in the same segment when the surface pattern is VERB + (DET/ADJ*) NOUN (optionally parenthetical/Acronym).

example_pair.input: Dr. Tony Moll discovered the Extremely Drug Resistant Tuberculosis (XDR-TB) in the South African region KwaZulu-Natal.
example_pair.output: Dr. Tony Moll discovered the Extremely Drug Resistant Tuberculosis (XDR-TB) <SEG:1> in the South African region KwaZulu-Natal.

cases.span: Inuit in Canada and Kalaalleq (plural Kalaallit),
cases.evidence: Boundary after 'Inuit' caused the locative/appositive to attach incorrectly; the translation needed the following PP/appositive to resolve scope.
cases.proposed_rule: Avoid cutting immediately after an ethnonym/demonym token when it is followed by a locative prepositional phrase starting with 'in' or by a comma-elided appositive; include the following PP/appositive in the same piece so the demonym's scope is settled.

example_pair.input: The native inhabitants of Greenland call themselves Inuit in Canada and Kalaalleq (plural Kalaallit), a Greenlander, in Greenland.
example_pair.output: The native inhabitants of Greenland call themselves Inuit in Canada and Kalaalleq (plural Kalaallit), a Greenlander, in Greenland.<SEG:1>

cases.evidence: High contradiction on pieces ending at commas; audit shows comma-boundaries are on average ranked too confident (feature '뒤 구두점 ","' over_trust = 0.2249).
cases.proposed_rule: Lower the confidence (rank) of candidate boundaries that end at a comma when the preceding fragment is an incomplete predicate or when the following material begins with a temporal/locative PP or a coordinating conjunction — keep the comma candidate but rank it lower so it is chosen only with sufficient budget.

example_pair.input: Downhill skiing as a sport goes back to at least the 17th century, and in 1861 the first recreational ski club was opened by Norwegians in Australia.
example_pair.output: Downhill skiing as a sport goes back to at least the 17th century, and in 1861 the first recreational ski club was opened by Norwegians in Australia.<SEG:1>

summary: The prompt is allowing boundaries that isolate verb complements or ethnonyms before their disambiguating modifiers, causing real mistranslations. It also over-trusts comma-ending candidates: comma splits are frequently ranked too high even when the following PP/appositive or conjunction is needed to settle scope. Apply the two placement rules to keep verbs with their objects and keep demonyms with their locatives/appositives, and demote (not ban) comma-ending candidates when they follow incomplete predicates or precede PPs/conjunctions.

aggregate.dominant_basis: No corpus rate identifies a dominant failure. Read the cases and `judge_distribution` for WHICH mechanism to fix — do not infer a rate from `case_label_counts`, those cases were selected for being the worst.

coverage.of: all sentences scored — a true corpus rate
coverage.meaning: sentences where the tightest budget asked for boundaries the prompt never marked, so pieces are missing outright

premature_among_judged.of: boundaries judged this iteration, selected as the WORST by measured contradiction — NOT a corpus rate, do not compare it against `coverage`

case_label_counts.of: the selected worst cases — NOT a rate
